stem: Which nursing action best demonstrates therapeutic use of self in a mental health setting?

options.A: Use frequent personal self-disclosure to create a friendship and make the relationship less professionally bounded.
options.B: Remain emotionally detached and avoid reflecting on personal reactions so the nurse's self never enters the interaction.
options.C: Use self-awareness, purposeful presence, empathy, therapeutic communication, and professional boundaries to support the client's therapeutic goals.
options.D: Agree with the client's beliefs and decisions automatically even when doing so conflicts with therapeutic goals or professional judgment.

rationale: Current Open RN/NCBI mental-health nursing guidance describes the therapeutic nurse-client relationship as a purposeful professional relationship focused on client needs and goals. Effective therapeutic communication includes self-awareness, client-centered active listening and empathy, intentional presence, and maintenance of professional boundaries; personal self-disclosure and boundary blurring are identified as barriers. Therefore C best demonstrates therapeutic use of self. A blurs professional boundaries, B rejects the reflective self-awareness and therapeutic presence needed for the relationship, and D substitutes indiscriminate agreement for therapeutic communication and professional judgment.
educational_objective: Use self-awareness, purposeful presence, empathy, therapeutic communication, and professional boundaries intentionally to advance the client's therapeutic goals rather than creating a social friendship or withdrawing emotionally.
source_organization: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN Nursing: Mental Health and Community Concepts
source_document_title: Therapeutic Communication and the Nurse-Client Relationship, 2nd edition
source_version_date: 2nd edition published November 1, 2025; currentness live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Chapter 2 > Nurse-Client Relationship: therapeutic relationship is compassionate, supportive, professional, establishes trust/rapport with a specific purpose and supports client goals. Therapeutic Communication/Tips for Effective Therapeutic Communication: establish a goal; be self-aware; be client-centered; provide empathy; use active listening; avoid personal self-disclosure; maintain professional boundaries. Common Barriers: lack of awareness of personal biases/feelings and blurring nurse-client boundaries.
source_claim_supported: Therapeutic use of self is intentional, self-aware, client-centered professional engagement using empathy, presence, communication, and boundaries to support client goals; friendship-seeking disclosure, detachment, and boundary blurring are nontherapeutic.

source_original.stem: Which nursing action best demonstrates therapeutic use of self in a mental health setting?

options.A: Use frequent personal self-disclosure to create a friendship and make the relationship less professionally bounded.
options.B: Remain emotionally detached and avoid reflecting on personal reactions so the nurse's self never enters the interaction.
options.C: Use self-awareness, presence, empathy, therapeutic communication, and professional boundaries to support the client's goals.
options.D: Agree with the client's beliefs and decisions even when they conflict with therapeutic goals or professional judgment.

source_original.rationale: Therapeutic use of self involves intentional, self-aware use of presence, empathy, communication, and professional boundaries to support the client's therapeutic goals. Option C is correct. Extensive self-disclosure, emotional detachment, and indiscriminate agreement undermine the therapeutic relationship.
source_original.source_detail: Psychosocial Integrity activity statements/content examples: establish therapeutic relationships using therapeutic communication, support client coping and psychosocial needs, and maintain professional boundaries while providing client-centered care. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. correction_summary: Retained the therapeutic-use-of-self construct and key C, upgraded the clinical source from blueprint-only NCSBN wording to current 2025 Open RN/NCBI mental-health nursing content that directly supports self-awareness, empathy, purposeful communication, client goals, and professional boundaries, and tightened distractor D to distinguish empathy from automatic agreement.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Therapeutic use of self in mental-health nursing
audit_findings.source_authority: Current NCBI/Open RN mental-health nursing text for clinical construct; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: Open RN 2nd edition published 2025-11-01 and current in NCBI Bookshelf; live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: Chapter 2 > Nurse-Client Relationship, Therapeutic Communication, Tips for Effective Therapeutic Communication, and Common Barriers
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses directly supported therapeutic-relationship principles: purpose, self-awareness, empathy/client-centered listening, presence, communication, and professional boundaries. It avoids claiming that therapeutic use of self requires personal disclosure or emotional detachment.

distractor_audit.A: Frequent personal disclosure/friendship blurs professional boundaries and shifts the relationship away from therapeutic goals.
distractor_audit.B: Emotional detachment and refusal to reflect on personal reactions conflict with self-awareness, presence, and client-centered engagement.
distractor_audit.C: Correct and directly supported by current mental-health nursing guidance.
distractor_audit.D: Automatic agreement is not therapeutic communication and can conflict with client goals and professional judgment.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C combines reflective self-awareness with purposeful client-centered engagement and professional boundaries.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives describe relational nursing behaviors; the correct answer is not identified by an unrelated safety rule or diagnosis.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity — therapeutic relationship, communication, coping support, and professional boundaries.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current Open RN/NCBI Chapter 2, all alternatives, rationale, objective, NCSBN blueprint alignment, ambiguity and cueing. C remained uniquely correct.
